author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jake Woodford to sign majors deal with Cubs
desc: The Cubs are reportedly signing right-hander Jake Woodford to a big-league deal on Saturday.
impact: Woodford was designated for assignment by the Brewers before clearing waivers and electing free agency versus a minor league assignment in early June. The 29-year-old struggled to a 6.94 ERA in 16 outings with the Brewers this season and owns a 5.25 ERA across 127 outings (25 starts) since entering the big leagues in the 2020 season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Brandon Nimmo (shoulder) returns to starting lineup Saturday
desc: Rangers outfielder Brandon Nimmo (shoulder) is back in the starting lineup Saturday, hitting fourth and playing right field.
impact: Nimmo has been out of the lineup with a shoulder injury after crashing into the wall while making a catch to end a win over the Blue Jays on June 28. The veteran has hit .262 with eight homers, 35 runs, 29 RBI, three stolen bases, and a .753 OPS across 82 games in his first season with the Rangers after an off-season deal from the Mets.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Eliezer Alfonzo called up to the bigs
desc: The Dodgers are calling up catcher Eliezer Alfonzo Jr. from Triple-A Oklahoma City.
impact: Alfonza joined the Dodgers as a minor-league free agent this past winter and has had a nice showing with Oklahoma City, hitting .313 with an .814 OPS across 49 games. Will Smith (neck) isn't ready to return from the injured list yet, so it's likely Alfonzo could see his big-league debut this weekend.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Kumar Rocker to start Sunday versus Tigers
desc: Rangers right-hander Kumar Rocker will start Sunday's series finale against the Tigers.
impact: Rocker was originally scheduled as Saturday's starter, but he will switch spots with Cal Quantrill and pitch on Sunday instead. The right-hander has had a solid season, posting a 3.83 ERA across 14 starts (16 appearances), altough he is just 2-6 to show for it.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Cal Quantrill to start Saturday versus Tigers
desc: Rangers right-hander Cal Quantrill will start Saturday's game against the Tigers.
impact: Quantrill was originally slated to start Sunday's contest, but will flip spots with Kumar Rocker, who was scheduled as Saturday's starter but will now pitch Sunday. Quantrill has posted a rock-solid 3.31 ERA in 17 outings (two starts) across 35 1/3 innings for the Rangers this season, although his 5.15 xFIP and 4.61 SIERA suggest he's been rather fortunate to post that figure.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tommy Kahnle elects free agency
desc: Tommy Kahnle has elected free agency.
impact: Kahnle will be free to sign with any team.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Griffin Canning to pitch in bulk relief role Saturday
desc: Griffin Canning will pitch in a bulk relief role on Saturday against the Dodgers.
impact: Canning has continued to struggle on the mound this season. He will follow Wandy Peralta as the opener.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Wandy Peralta to open for Padres Saturday
desc: Wandy Peralta will serve as the opener for the Padres on Saturday against the Dodgers.
impact: Peralta will pitch the first inning or two. Griffin Canning will follow him on the mound.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Sean Sullivan to start Saturday versus Giants
desc: Rockies left-hander Sean Sullivan will start Saturday's game against the Giants in place of Tomoyuki Sugano (back).
impact: Sugano was scratched on Saturday due to back spasms, as Sullivan will make his fifth start of the season in his place. The southpaw has been roughed up for an 8.64 ERA through four starts with the Rockies this season and also owns a 5.60 ERA across 11 starts for Triple-A Albuquerque.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Max Fried (elbow) to throw 35 pitches in live BP session Sunday
desc: Max Fried is scheduled for another 35-pitch live BP session on Sunday.
impact: If all goes well, the next step for Fried could be going on a rehab assignment. He is expected to make his return in August.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Tomoyuki Sugano (back) scratched from start Saturday
desc: Rockies right-hander Tomoyuki Sugano has been scratched from Saturday's start against the Giants due to back spasms.
impact: Sugano was scheduled to make a home start against the Giants on Saturday evening, but it will be left-hander Sean Sullivan taking his place. Sugano had also been dealing with a finger issue after being shelled for seven earned runs against the Twins his last time out. It's unclear when Sugano's next turn through the rotation will come, as he sports a 4.80 ERA and a 48:20 K:BB through 16 starts and 84 1/3 innings this season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Kade Anderson continues to dominate in Double-A
desc: Kade Anderson allowed two runs over six innings with nine strikeouts n Friday for Double-A Arkansas.
impact: Anderson has now posted a dominant 1.36 ERA with 108 strikeouts across 72 2/3 innings over 14 starts this season. He will headline the American League's roster at the All-Star Futures Game. He should get his chance in the majors with the Mariners at some point later this year.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Brenton Doyle (oblique/groin) hits home run in rehab game Friday
desc: Brenton Doyle went 2-for-5 with a solo homer on Friday in a rehab game for Triple-A Albuquerque.
impact: Doyle resumed his rehab assignment on Friday after missing time earlier this week. He will likely be activated next week.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Munetaka Murakami (hamstring) close to starting rehab assignment
desc: The White Sox say Munetaka Murakami is close to starting a rehab assignment.
impact: Murakami was able to take batting practice on the field on Thursday. He'll still need to run the bases before he is cleared to go on a rehab assignment.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Dylan Cease dominates Mariners for fifth win Friday
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease pitched seven shutout innings while striking out nine to earn the win over the Mariners on Friday.
impact: Cease was purely dominant in this one, yielding just three hits and one walk to go along with nine strikeouts while notching his fifth win of the season. He threw 70 of his 102 pitches for strikes on the evening while facing just three batters over the minimum in his seven innings of work. The star right-hander has been as advertised in his first season with the Blue Jays, posting a 2.79 ERA and a massive 137:41 K:BB across 16 starts and 90 1/3 innings of work. He lines up to take on the Giants in a favorable road start in San Francisco on Wednesday.
